sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Anurag Shrivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Anurag Shrivastava, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Yogesh Srivastava,
learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.271 of 2022 registered under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 308 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act at Police Station- Dhampur, District Bijnor with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

4. As per prosecution story, the marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the daughter of the informant about two years before the date of occurrence and the applicant and other family Suresh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18829184/
1 members are stated to have subjected her to cruelty and caused injuries to her on 4.8.2022 at about 8 p.m. and had sent her off from their house, whereby the informant had taken his daughter back to his ancestral home.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The FIR is delayed by four days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

Initially the FIR was instituted under Sections 498-A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, but subsequently a new occurrence has been shown by the informant regarding the applicant and other family members having come to the house of the informant and caused injuries to his daughter,
whereby there are allegations against the applicant of having hit her in abdomen by a knife on 12.08.2022 at about 9:00 a.m.
The said occurrence cannot be added in the said FIR under any tenements of law.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that there is no such possibility of the applicant and other family members going all the way to the house of the informant from their house and committing the said offence.
The said allegations have been inflated just to somehow sent the applicant behind the bars.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There are no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel for the applicant undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.

7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application on the ground that under the provisions of Section 220 Cr.P.C., the matter can be added to the instant FIR,
although he could not dispute the fact that the said occurrence is stated to have happened at the house of the informant, which happens to be the maternal house of the victim.

8. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of theSupreme Court.
9. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

Let the accused-applicant-Suresh be released forthwith in the aforesaid case crime (supra) on anticipatory bail till the conclusion of trial on furnishing a personal and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i). that the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
